analysis:
Reviewed new Gemma4 tensor-parallel prefix and request-loop files. The resident runtime unit (f8ba385129dbab2b:0) supplied metadata only; its 567 added lines were not visible, so wiring is unreviewed.

Gemma4TensorParallelPrefix.swift: tenant isolation (T-041, A-001) depends on ClusterWorkerPrefixCache.scope(..., request.prefixCache) at lines 69-72. The resident scope is load|gemma4-tp-prefix-v1|chunk. The disk scope is planScope|chunk|kv=paged. scopes() returns nil when the cache is disabled or the scope is nil (line 68-70), and nil disables both tiers. Not visible: whether request.prefixCache carries the coordinator-authored account salt, and whether a nil or empty salt is refused rather than shared.

The SSD tier (QwenStagePrefixDiskTier: restore, persist, touch, forget) is used at lines 115-124, 190 and 254. Its encryption, HMAC naming and TTL are outside the supplied evidence. adopts() (134-151) checks shape and dtype before restore. An SSD state is inserted into the resident tier when this rank restored, even without both ranks confirming (199-201); this is documented behavior.

The vote and confirm steps (89-103, 195) share per-rank hit bits only within the sealed TP pair. This leaks nothing new beyond the accepted same-scope TTFT oracle in SEC-035.

Threat-model gap to confirm in integration: T-041 states that production creates no resident-RAM prefix tier. This cluster runtime keeps a resident QwenStagePrefixCache (lines 252, 200). It appears to mirror the existing Gemma pipeline pattern rather than introduce a new class of exposure, but the threat model does not explicitly cover cluster-runtime prefix tiers.

RequestLoop.swift: token publish, stop and reconcile logic (lines 66-154) has no plaintext or authorization surface. Rank 1 adopts rank 0's count and finish via exchange (142-148).

Integration should verify:
- ResidentRuntime construction of the prefix (load agreement, diskPlanScope, KEK-backed disk tier).
- Kill-switch handling (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE).
- prefixCache scope derivation from the coordinator cacheSalt.
